notes: Located Baiyun District, Guangzhou. Phase I operational since 2006. Combined among the larger plants in Guangdong. Biogenic ~50%. Weak storage/regulatory context.

operator: Hangzhou Linjiang Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.

name: Osaka Maishima WtE Facility
capacity_note: 300,000 t/yr MSW; 32 MW
source: Power Technology Maishima profile; Industry About Osaka Maishima; GEM Maishima power station

name: Seoul Mapo Resource Recovery Facility

source: Seoul Solution Mapo Resource Recovery Facility article; Korea Times 2020

name: Avertas Energy Kwinana WtE (formerly Kwinana EfW)

Emissions estimate based on industry benchmarks (~1.8 tCO2/t pulp for recovery boiler + biomass boiler combined). Storage risk: Sumatra has limited proximate geological storage; thesis sourcing-risk flag applies.

name: APP Indah Kiat Serang Paper Mill

name: Tjiwi Kimia Paper Mill (APP)
capacity_note: ~1.2 Mt/yr paper + board; ~320,000 t/yr stationery converting
operator: PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia Tbk (APP Sinar Mas)

name: Nine Dragons Paper Dongguan Mill
capacity_note: 5.85 Mt/yr (16 paper machines); world's largest single-site containerboard complex
source: Nine Dragons Dongguan Base page; Wikipedia Nine Dragons Paper Holdings; GEM Lee & Man Paper power station (comparable facility cross-check)

CO2 estimate is conservative. Weak storage pipeline—Guangdong offshore basins in early development.

name: Sun Paper Group Yanzhou Mill

name: Chenming Paper Shouguang (Meilun) Mill

name: Nippon Paper Ishinomaki Mill
capacity_note: 643,000 t/yr woodpulp; 370,000 t/yr DIP; ~1.1 Mt/yr paper
source: Andritz Nippon Paper spectrum article; Nippon Paper Group domestic mills page; GEM Ishinomaki Mill power station
notes: Ishinomaki City, Miyagi Prefecture. Large kraft pulp mill with integrated recovery boilers — concentrated biogenic CO2. Japan government has CCS roadmap targeting offshore geological storage.

name: Oji Paper Tomakomai Mill
capacity_note: >1 Mt/yr paper (11 machines); world's largest newsprint mill
source: Oji Paper Andritz profile; Wikimapia Oji Paper Tomakomai Mill; GEM Tomakomai power station
notes: Oji-machi 2-chome, Tomakomai, Hokkaido. Operational since 1910; now world's largest newsprint mill. Large recovery boilers and biomass power plant on-site. Tomakomai has Japan's only operating CCS pilot (METI/JCCS) — high retrofit strategic value.

name: Nippon Paper Yatsushiro Mill
capacity_note: est. 400,000–600,000 t/yr pulp and paper
source: Nippon Paper Group domestic mills page; Andritz Nippon Paper spectrum
notes: Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu. One of Nippon Paper's integrated kraft mills. Capacity estimate approximate — Nippon Paper does not publish per-mill capacity publicly.

name: Daio Paper Mishima Mill

source: Daio Paper key locations page; GEM Daio Mishima Mill power station; JSTAGE Mishima Mill article

name: ITC Bhadrachalam Paperboards & Specialty Papers

name: JK Paper Mills Rayagada (JKPM)

Gippsland has potential offshore storage in Bass Strait; high retrofit score.

Potential storage in Gunnedah Basin or offshore Otway. High retrofit score: single-site large source, private operator with sustainability commitments.
